posts.title: Romance Recent Reads
posts.description: Thrown For a Loop by Sarina Bowen (2025) Chase and Zoe met and fell in love at figure skating camp - fast forward 10 years, they are reuniting as star hockey player and skating coach. Even though things ended badly, Zoe is determined to be professional, and when they end up working closely together on a charity fundraiser, they start to feel those old feelings again. I thought this was a cute read - the two timelines had very different feels, though. The present day POV is Zoe's, and the past chapters are told from Chase's 3rd-person POV. I appreciated the initial tension between Zoe and Chase, although I did feel like their second-chance romance came about very abruptly (especially considering Zoe's stance on not dating team players). I'm not a big hockey fan, but I liked all the sports stuff, and Bowen did a great job regarding Zoe's coaching position - she really made her seem professional and knowledgeable. 4 stars Romantic Hero by Kirsty Greenwood (2026) Gertie is a romance author

posts.title: Recent Reads
posts.description: A Rather Peculiar Poisoning by Chrystal Schleyer (2025) Twins Easton and Weston both love Eloise, but while she loves Weston back, she is engaged to Easton. Weston is engaged to an heiress. While the entire group is brought together to celebrate the engagements, there are several attempts on Weston's life. Who would want Weston dead, and why? I was intrigued by this premise, but unfortunately this turned out to be a "meh" mystery for me. I admit, I was surprised by the ending and didn't see it coming, although it did feel a bit heavy-handed. But the route it took there was so circuitous and repetitive. There are several POVs, intriguingly all women and never the two men who are central to the story, but I really had to keep reminding myself who was the focus of each chapter. The writing was a bit overdone and the constant comparing of things like sweaters to food was a little odd, and the constant moving between timelines was a struggle. 3 stars Warm Bodies by John Marrs (2026) Brenda
